claude.rationale: gap_45=0: the acquired product lines (masterbatch, engineered plastics, engineered composites) and the legal vehicle with its 54 manufacturing facilities and ~5,200 employees crossed intact as a wholly owned subsidiary, so product and its producing/delivering operations moved together with no documented product-vs-process mismatch at closing. gap_56=1: the operating processes crossed inside the surviving subsidiary, but the top organization/management layer was replaced at the effective time — the entire pre-merger board plus CEO/COO/CFO resigned and were replaced by the acquirer's designated officers/directors, a structural T5-without-coherent-T6 mismatch. gap_mitigated=yes: the deal contractually absorbed the people substrate via a one-year "Continuation Period" guaranteeing continuing employees no-less-favorable compensation, benefits, severance, and service credit, allocating the shared employee substrate at closing.

gemini.rationale: The evidence states that A. Schulman's product lines and 54 manufacturing facilities crossed intact to the acquirer, indicating no structural mismatch between product and process (gap_45 = 0). Similarly, the rank-and-file employees ('continuing Company employee') transferred alongside these operations, meaning the organization aligned with the processes at closing (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: The structural summary and closing 8-K establish that the legal vehicle together with its product lines (masterbatch, engineered plastics, engineered composites) and the underlying manufacturing footprint crossed intact as a wholly owned subsidiary, so T4 and T5 moved together and gap_45=0. Rank-and-file continuing employees remained with the surviving entity under a one-year compensation/benefits continuation covenant while only the pre-merger board and named CEO/COO/CFO were replaced at the effective time; that is ordinary control substitution, not a documented processes-without-organization mismatch at closing, so gap_56=0.
